correctness.rationale: The explicit cubic graph and open-neighbor rule define the full 4096-state deterministic map. Exhaustive independent enumeration of first repeats gives the (period 1, period 2) entry rows (16,274), (136,994), (492,708), (360,252), (432,144), (216,72) at t=0 through 5. Grouping by the repeated suffix up to cyclic rotation yields all published fixed and two-cycle basin sizes and multiplicities, including both unanimous basins of 776. The maximum entry of 5 and period bound 2 imply F^7=F^5; 31→198→22→192→16→0→0 refutes F^6=F^4. An exhaustive action of the 12 edge-preserving permutations gives six fixed and 29 two-cycle spatial classes. Independently, contraction of the unique triangle identifies the automorphism group with a vertex stabilizer in the Petersen group S5 (recognizable from the five maximum independent stars in KG(5,2)); this stabilizer has order 2!3!=12.
residual_risks: Finite labelled classification only, for the stated synchronous rule; no formal proof-assistant or expert attestation is asserted.

value.rationale: The Tietze graph is a standard cubic comparison to the Petersen graph, not an arbitrary choice of a twelve-vertex example. Its triangle inflation increases the exact worst settling time from four to five and substantially changes the recurrent and basin counts. The basin and symmetry tables distinguish that concrete change in local dynamics beyond the classical period bound and are independently useful as canonical test cases.
residual_risks: Does not imply a trend for arbitrary triangle inflations or cubic graphs.
